original_text: Referring to previous studies \citep{2024ApJ...968L..25B,2024RAA....24d5013Z}, we model the detections using binomial statistics and adopt a flat prior on the conditional frequency.
injected_text: Referring to previous studies \citep{2024ApJ...968L..25B,2024RAA....24d5013Z}, we model the detections using Poisson statistics and adopt a flat prior on the conditional frequency.
rationale: Bryan & Lee (2024) and Zhu (2024) explicitly use a binomial likelihood for detection counts in fixed-size system samples (yielding a Beta-distribution posterior), not Poisson statistics; swapping 'binomial' to 'Poisson' mis-categorizes the statistical model at the method-category level while keeping the general topic (counting-based inference) plausible.
ground_truth_description: Changed 'binomial statistics' to 'Poisson statistics' in the method description citing Bryan & Lee 2024 and Zhu 2024, incorrectly categorizing their binomial likelihood / Beta-posterior approach as Poisson-based.

rationale: Flipping the exponent from b-1 to 1-b in the beta-distribution PDF makes the density diverge as P→1 (giving ∞) instead of vanishing (the correct limit is 0 for b>1), so the equation encodes a patently false limit claim that Wolfram's Limit[] immediately refutes.
ground_truth_description: The exponent of (1-P) in the posterior beta-distribution PDF was changed from b-1 to 1-b, reversing the boundary behaviour at P→1 from the correct limit of 0 to the false limit of ∞.
